sentences.en: From The New York Times, this is The Interview.
sentences.zh: 来自《纽约时报》，这里是《访谈》。

sentences.en: I'm Gilbert Cruz.
sentences.zh: 我是吉尔伯特·克鲁兹。

sentences.en: I'm guest hosting this week, filling in for Lulu.
sentences.zh: 我是本周的客座主持，代班露露。

sentences.en: If you don't know me, I'm the editor of The New York Times Book Review and the host of The Book Review podcaSt.
sentences.zh: 如果您还不认识我，我是《纽约时报书评》的编辑兼《书评》播客的主持人。

sentences.en: and I'm very happy to be getting the chance to talk with author Isabel Allende.
sentences.zh: 我非常高兴能有机会与作家伊莎贝尔·阿连德对话。

sentences.en: At 82, Allende is one of the world's most beloved and best-selling Spanish language authors.
sentences.zh: 82岁的阿连德是世界上最受喜爱、最畅销的西班牙语作家之一。

sentences.en: Her work has been translated into more than 40 languages and 80 million copies of her books have been sold around the world.
sentences.zh: 她的作品已被翻译成40多种语言，在全球售出了8000万册。

sentences.en: Allende's newest book is called My Name is Emilia Del Valle and it's about a dark period in Chilean history, the 1891 Chilean Civil War.
sentences.zh: 阿连德最新的一本书名为《我叫艾米莉亚·德尔瓦莱》，讲述了智利历史上的一个黑暗时期，即1891年的智利内战。

sentences.en: Like so much of Allende's work, it's a story about women in tough spots who figure out a way through.
sentences.zh: 就像阿连德的大多数作品一样，这是一个关于身处困境的女性如何找到出路的故事。

sentences.en: It's not that far off from Allende's own story.
sentences.zh: 这离阿连德自己的故事并不遥远。

sentences.en: She was raised in Chile, but in 1973, when she was 31 and working as a journalist with two small children, her life was upended forever.
sentences.zh: 她在智利长大，但在1973年，当她31岁并作为一名记者、带着两个幼儿时，她的人生被永远颠覆了。

sentences.en: It was then that a military coup pushed out the democratically elected president, Salvador Allende, who was her cousin.
sentences.zh: 正是在那时，一场军事政变推翻了通过民主选举上台的总统萨尔瓦多·阿连德，他是她的堂兄。

sentences.en: She fled to Venezuela, where she wrote her first book, The House of the Spirits, which evolved from a letter she had started to her dying grandfather.
sentences.zh: 她逃往委内瑞拉，并在那里写下了她的第一本书《幽灵之家》，这本书是从她写给垂死祖父的一封信演变而来的。

sentences.en: That book became a runaway bestseller, and it remains one of her best-known works.
sentences.zh: 那本书一跃成为畅销书，至今仍是她最著名的作品之一。

sentences.en: She moved to the U.S.
sentences.zh: 她搬到了美国。

sentences.en: in the late 1980s, where she has been writing steadily ever since.
sentences.zh: 在20世纪80年代末，并在那里一直笔耕不辍至今。

sentences.en: Here is my conversation with Isabel Allende.
sentences.zh: 以下是我与伊莎贝尔·阿连德的对话。

sentences.en: personal history, and of course about writing and creativity.
sentences.zh: 个人历史，当然还有关于写作和创造力。

sentences.en: And I think for you, all of these things intertwine in many of your books, and they certainly do in your new novel.
sentences.zh: 我认为对你而言，所有这些事物在你的许多书中都交织在一起，在你的新小说中更是如此。

sentences.en: This is a book that is set in the 1890s.
sentences.zh: 这本书以19世纪90年代为背景。

sentences.en: Your main character heads down to witness the Chilean Civil War that is happening there.
sentences.zh: 你的主角前往现场去见证那里发生的智利内战。

sentences.en: And I'm wondering what was going through your mind when you said, this is the time period, this is the event, and this is what I want my character to see.
sentences.zh: 我想知道当你说“这就是时间段，这就是事件，这就是我想让我的角色看到的”时，你心里在想什么。

sentences.en: I'm fascinated with history.
sentences.zh: 我对历史着迷。

sentences.en: Most of my schooling was done abroad, so I studied very little Chilean history, but I have studied it as an adult.
sentences.zh: 我的大部分学业都是在国外完成的，所以我对智利历史学得很少，但我成年后一直在研究它。

sentences.en: I look back all the time to what happened before in order to explain what's happening today in our lives.
sentences.zh: 我总是回顾过去发生的事情，以便解释今天我们生活中发生的事情。

sentences.en: There are some parallels between what happened in 1891, when the president, José Manuel Balmaceda, was challenged by his economic and political enemies of the conservative party.
sentences.zh: 1891年发生的事情与现在有一些相似之处，当时总统何塞·曼努埃尔·巴尔马塞达受到了保守党经济和政治敌人的挑战。
zh_words: 何塞·曼努埃尔·巴尔马塞达

sentences.en: The Navy went with the opposition, and then they had a civil war.
sentences.zh: 海军站在了反对派一边，然后他们爆发了内战。

sentences.en: It was brutal, brutal, bloody.
sentences.zh: 那是残酷的，极其残酷，血腥的。

sentences.en: And it has some parallels with what happened in 1973 in Chile with Salvador Allende.
sentences.zh: 它与1973年智利萨尔瓦多·阿连德身上发生的事情有一些相似之处。

sentences.en: There was no civil war.
sentences.zh: 当时并没有内战。

sentences.en: There was really a brutal military coup, as we know.
sentences.zh: 正如我们所知，那其实是一场残酷的军事政变。

sentences.en: But both presidents committed suicide.
sentences.zh: 但两位总统都自杀了。

sentences.en: In both circumstances, many Chileans died.
sentences.zh: 在两种情况下，许多智利人都死了。

sentences.en: So there were some historical parallels.
sentences.zh: 所以有一些历史相似之处。

sentences.en: So it was fascinating to explore.
sentences.zh: 因此探索起来非常引人入胜。

sentences.en: The main character, Emilia, she shares a last name of several other characters across your body of work, including several in your first book, The House of the Spirits.
sentences.zh: 主角艾米莉亚，她和你作品中其他几位角色的姓氏相同，包括你第一本书《幽灵之家》中的好几位。

sentences.en: Why does this name resonate with you?
sentences.zh: 为什么这个名字对你如此有共鸣？

sentences.en: What are you trying to say by sort of threading this name or this family line throughout several of your books?
sentences.zh: 通过在你的几本书中贯穿这个名字或这个家族血脉，你到底想表达什么？

sentences.en: You know, some characters, like some people, never leave you.
sentences.zh: 你知道，有些角色就像某些人一样，永远不会离开你。

sentences.en: I wrote The House of the Spirits inspired by my relatives from my grandmother's side, mostly.
sentences.zh: 我写《幽灵之家》的灵感主要来自于我祖母那边的亲戚。

sentences.en: And they were all lunatics and wonderful, extravagant people.
sentences.zh: 他们都是疯子，而且是极好、极其夸张的人。

sentences.en: I call them Del Valle, but really their last name is Barros.
sentences.zh: 我称他们为德尔瓦莱，但其实他们的姓氏是巴罗斯。

sentences.en: And so I picked up those characters, some of them, and there were many others there that I didn't have enough pages for them.
sentences.zh: 所以我挑选了那些角色，其中的一部分，还有许多其他角色，因为篇幅不够我没能写进去。

sentences.en: So they came back in other books.
sentences.zh: 所以他们在其他的书中又回来了。

sentences.en: Look, with relatives like mine, you don't need to invent anything.
sentences.zh: 听着，有我这样的亲戚，你根本不需要发明任何东西。

sentences.en: So the Del Valle family will be haunting me forever.
sentences.zh: 所以德尔瓦莱家族将永远萦绕在我心头。

sentences.en: Well, speaking of relatives, Emilia, she doesn't have a relationship with her birth father.
sentences.zh: 说到亲戚，艾米莉亚，她和她的亲生父亲没有任何关系。

sentences.en: She goes looking for him.
sentences.zh: 她去寻找他。

sentences.en: I know you did not have a relationship with your birth father.
sentences.zh: 我知道你和你的亲生父亲没有任何关系。

sentences.en: I'm curious about how your mother, Panchita, talked about your father when you were young and how you thought about him, if at all?
sentences.zh: 我很好奇，当你年轻时，你的母亲潘奇塔是如何谈论你父亲的？你是怎么看待他的（如果你曾想过的话）？

sentences.en: She never spoke about him.
sentences.zh: 她从不谈论他。

sentences.en: All the photographs in which he appeared were destroyed.
sentences.zh: 所有出现他形象的照片都被销毁了。

sentences.en: And there was never a mention of his name.
sentences.zh: 而且从来没有人提及他的名字。

sentences.en: And when we asked, she would always say he was a very intelligent man.
sentences.zh: 当我们追问时，她总是说他是一个非常聪明的人。

sentences.en: That's it.
sentences.zh: 就这样。

sentences.en: She wouldn't say why he left, why we couldn't see him.
sentences.zh: 她不会说他为什么离开，为什么我们不能见他。

sentences.en: No explanation.
sentences.zh: 没有任何解释。

sentences.en: At some point, when they were teenagers, my brothers wanted to meet him.
sentences.zh: 有一次，当他们还是青少年时，我的兄弟们想见他。

sentences.en: And it was a big disappointment for them because my father had absolutely no connection with them and no interest in them.
sentences.zh: 对他们来说这是一个巨大的失望，因为我父亲和他们完全没有任何联系，对他们也没有兴趣。

sentences.en: But I never looked for them.
sentences.zh: 但我从来没有去找过他们。

sentences.en: And many years later, when I was working as a journalist, I was called to the morgue to identify a body of a man that had died in the street.
sentences.zh: 多年后，当我当记者时，我被叫去停尸房辨认一具死在街上的男子的尸体。

sentences.en: And I couldn't identify him because I had never seen a picture of him.
sentences.zh: 我没能认出他，因为我从未见过他的照片。

sentences.en: That was my father.
sentences.zh: 那个人就是我父亲。

sentences.en: First of all, that sounds terrible.
sentences.zh: 首先，听起来太可怕了。

sentences.en: No, it wasn't terrible because, I mean, it was terrible to see a corpse for the first time.
sentences.zh: 不，并不可怕，我是说，第一次看到尸体确实挺可怕。

sentences.en: But I didn't feel anything, any connection, any compassion, any longing of any kind.
sentences.zh: 但我没有感受到任何东西，没有任何联系，没有任何同情，没有任何形式的渴望。

sentences.en: Emilia also doesn't have a connection to her father for much of her life.
sentences.zh: 在生命的大部分时间里，艾米莉亚和她的父亲也没有联系。

sentences.en: However, the scenes in the book when Emilia does finally meet her father, not to give away too many details, I found quite moving.
sentences.zh: 然而，书中艾米莉亚终于见到她父亲的那些场景——为了不剧透太多细节——我觉得非常感人。

sentences.en: And I was wondering what it was like to write those scenes for you.
sentences.zh: 我想知道对你来说，写那些场景是什么感觉。

sentences.en: I could put myself in her place.
sentences.zh: 我可以把自己代入她的位置。

sentences.en: I suppose that if I have met my father and he was an old man, sick, anxious, depressed, sad, fearing death,
sentences.zh: 我想，如果我见到了我的父亲，而他已经是一个老人，生病了、焦虑、沮丧、悲伤、害怕死亡，

sentences.en: I would feel compassion and I would feel close to him.
sentences.zh: 我会感到同情，并且会觉得和他很亲近。

sentences.en: But I never had that chance, so I don't know.
sentences.zh: 但我从来没有那个机会，所以我不知道。

sentences.en: But it was easy for me to imagine that she would behave like that because also she was very open-minded, Emilia.
sentences.zh: 但对我来说，想象她会那样做很容易，因为艾米莉亚也非常思想开放。

sentences.en: She was open to everything.
sentences.zh: 她对一切都持开放态度。

sentences.en: Emilia, not surprisingly, given who you are, she bucks a lot of convention for women of her time period.
sentences.zh: 考虑到你的身份，艾米莉亚打破了她那个时代女性的许多传统，这并不令人意外。

sentences.en: She goes on to become a war reporter.
sentences.zh: 她后来成为了一名战地记者。

sentences.en: She writes gory dime novels about murder and vengeance.
sentences.zh: 她撰写关于谋杀和复仇的血腥低俗小说。

sentences.en: You have written and you've said many times that you've been a feminist since you were a child because of the way that you saw your mother and women of your mother's generation treated when you were growing up in Chile.
sentences.zh: 你曾多次写过并说过，你从小就是个女权主义者，因为你在智利成长时，看到了你的母亲和她那一代女性所受到的对待。

sentences.en: And I wonder, over the course of your career, has it been purposeful to write your female characters in this way?
sentences.zh: 我想知道，在你的职业生涯中，以这种方式塑造你的女性角色是有意为之吗？

sentences.en: Or it's just like, this is the only way I know how to write women.
sentences.zh: 还是说，“这就是我唯一知道该如何描写女性的方式”？

sentences.en: You know, it would be very hard for me to write a novel about a submissive wife in the suburbs that waits for her husband to come back from the job.
sentences.zh: 你知道，要让我写一本关于郊区顺从妻子的长篇小说会很难，她只等着丈夫下班回家。

sentences.en: I mean, there's no story there.
sentences.zh: 我是说，那里面根本没有什么故事。

sentences.en: You really want your character.
sentences.zh: 你真的需要你的角色……

sentences.en: Look, you cannot have characters with common sense.
sentences.zh: 听着，你不能让角色拥有常识。

sentences.en: You cannot have characters who are like everybody else, who don't suffer.
sentences.zh: 你不能让角色变得和所有人一样，不会经受痛苦。

sentences.en: The stories in the tragedy, in the drama, in the struggle, in the hero's journey, that's where the story is.
sentences.zh: 故事就在悲剧、戏剧性、抗争以及英雄的旅程中，那才是故事所在的地方。

sentences.en: I write about women who are always challenging convention and get a lot of aggression for that, but they stand up and they are able to pen for themselves.
sentences.zh: 我写那些总是挑战传统并因此遭受大量攻击的女性，但她们挺身而出，能够为自己发声。

sentences.en: Those are the characters I love, and I write about them because I know them so well.
sentences.zh: 这些是我热爱的角色，我写她们是因为我太了解她们了。

sentences.en: And in many ways I can connect to that because I was born in a Catholic, conservative, authoritarian, patriarchal family in the 40s, in the middle of the Second World War,
sentences.zh: 在许多方面我都能对此产生共鸣，因为我在40年代第二次世界大战正酣时，出生在一个天主教、保守、威权、父权制的家庭里，

sentences.en: women of my generation and my social class were supposed to marry and have kids, and that's it.
sentences.zh: 我这一代人和我阶层的女性本该结婚生子，然后就结束了。

sentences.en: So to get out of that prison, really, of the mind, was very challenging.
sentences.zh: 所以要真正走出思想的那座监狱，是非常具有挑战性的。

sentences.en: I belonged to the first generation of women who were able, some of us, to do it.
sentences.zh: 我属于第一代能够——我们中的一些人——做到这一点的女性。

sentences.en: How old do you think you were when you realized it was a prison of sorts?
sentences.zh: 你觉得你大概多大时意识到那算是一种监狱？

sentences.en: Teenager.
sentences.zh: 青少年时期。

sentences.en: When I was little, I didn't want to be dependent.
sentences.zh: 自我很小的时候起，我就不想依附于人。

sentences.en: My mother says that when I was five or six, they would ask, what would you like to do when you grow up?
sentences.zh: 我母亲说，当我五六岁时，他们会问：“你长大后想做什么？”

sentences.en: And I would say, support myself.
sentences.zh: 而我会说：“养活自己。”

sentences.en: No.
sentences.zh: 不。

sentences.en: That was my answer.
sentences.zh: 那就是我的回答。

sentences.en: Support myself.
sentences.zh: 养活自己。

sentences.en: Because I realized that because my mother could not support herself, She depended on her father, her brother, other people, and that made her very vulnerable.
sentences.zh: 因为我意识到，由于我母亲无法养活自己，她必须依附于她的父亲、她的兄弟和其他人，这让她变得非常脆弱。

sentences.en: I didn't want that.
sentences.zh: 我不要那样。

sentences.en: But then later, I sort of targeted male authority.
sentences.zh: 但后来，我某种程度上把矛头指向了男权。

sentences.en: I realized that authority was always in the hands of men, the priests, the police, my grandfather.
sentences.zh: 我意识到权威总是掌握在男人手中，神父、警察、我的祖父。

sentences.en: It was always male.
sentences.zh: 权力永远属于男性。

sentences.en: And then I rebelled against that, but it didn't have a name.
sentences.zh: 然后我对此进行了反叛，但当时它还没有名字。

sentences.en: I didn't know that there was something called feminism.
sentences.zh: 我不知道有什么东西叫女权主义。

sentences.en: I had never heard the word.
sentences.zh: 我从未听过这个词。

sentences.en: And when I was in my late teens, then I heard about feminism and about the women's movement,
sentences.zh: 当我在十几岁快结束时，我听说了女权主义和妇女运动，

sentences.en: and I started reading a few things that gave me a more articulate language to express the anger that I had been feeling all my life.
sentences.zh: 我开始阅读一些书籍，这为我提供了一种更清晰的语言，来表达我一生中感受到的愤怒。

sentences.en: did you have other female friends who you could sort of talk to about this?
sentences.zh: 你有其他女性朋友可以和你谈论这些吗？

sentences.en: Not about this, no.
sentences.zh: 没有，谈论这个没有。

sentences.en: This is not great.
sentences.zh: 这可不太妙。

sentences.en: What's going on here?
sentences.zh: 这到底是怎么回事？

sentences.en: We got to break free.
sentences.zh: 我们得挣脱束缚。

sentences.en: I didn't because girls were into, I don't know, into trying to catch a husband, I suppose.
sentences.zh: 我没有，因为女孩们都在忙着，我不知道，忙着试图钓到一个丈夫吧，我想。

sentences.en: I don't know.
sentences.zh: 我不知道。

sentences.en: I found a community of women who thought alike when I started working as a journalist in a women's magazine called Paula.
sentences.zh: 当我开始在一家名为《保拉》的女性杂志担任记者时，我找到了一群志同道合的女性社区。

sentences.en: And it was a fascinating time because this was the first time in Chile there was a magazine that dared publish topics that had never been touched before.
sentences.zh: 那是一个迷人的时代，因为这是智利第一次出现敢于发表从未涉及过的话题的杂志。

sentences.en: So we talked about abortion, divorce, infidelity, all those things, plus politics.
sentences.zh: 所以我们讨论堕落、离婚、不忠，所有这些事情，还有政治。

sentences.en: So we got involved also in what was going on in the streets among people, you know.
sentences.zh: 所以我们也参与到了人们在街头所做的事情中，你知道的。

sentences.en: So it was, but we also had fashion and beauty and decoration.
sentences.zh: 所以，它不仅于此，我们也有时尚、美妆和家居装饰。

sentences.en: It was a glossy women's magazine.
sentences.zh: 这是一本光鲜亮丽的女性杂志。

sentences.en: But with all this information that women had not had before, it caused quite a stir.
sentences.zh: 但由于包含了女性以前从未获得过的大量信息，它引起了相当大的轰动。

sentences.en: It changed the culture.
sentences.zh: 它改变了文化。

sentences.en: Now, many years later, 50 years later, that magazine is considered an icon in the culture in Chile.
sentences.zh: 现在，多年以后，50年过去了，那本杂志被视为智利文化中的一个标志。

sentences.en: That's how important it was.
sentences.zh: 这就是它的重要性所在。

sentences.en: That must have been so exciting.
sentences.zh: 那一定非常令人兴奋。

sentences.en: I mean, how...
sentences.zh: 我是说，怎么……

sentences.en: Oh, it was fascinating.
sentences.zh: 哦，太迷人了。

sentences.en: How was it to find a place that you felt finally...
sentences.zh: 找到一个让你觉得终于……的地方是什么感觉？

sentences.en: Yeah, to find a place.
sentences.zh: 是的，找到一个归宿。

sentences.en: And all these women were young.
sentences.zh: 而且这些女性都很年轻。

sentences.en: They were all beautiful.
sentences.zh: 她们都很漂亮。

sentences.en: They were so daring.
sentences.zh: 她们是如此大胆。

sentences.en: It was just great.
sentences.zh: 那真是太棒了。

sentences.en: So early in your career, you were a journaliSt.
sentences.zh: 在你职业生涯的早期，你是一名记者。

sentences.en: You worked for this magazine, Paola, as well as several other places.
sentences.zh: 你曾在这本名为宝拉的杂志以及其他几个地方工作过。

sentences.en: And the story goes that you met one of the most famous Chilean writers of all time, the great Chilean poet.
sentences.zh: 据说你遇到了有史以来最著名的智利作家之一，这位伟大的智利诗人。

sentences.en: Pablo Neruda.
sentences.zh: 巴勃罗·聂鲁达。

sentences.en: And he said, Isabel, maybe this is it for you.
sentences.zh: 他说，伊莎贝尔，也许这就是你的归宿了。

sentences.en: Well, he was living in the beach in Isla Negra.
sentences.zh: 当时他住在黑岛的海滩上。

sentences.en: He was sick and he already had won the Nobel Prize.
sentences.zh: 他生病了，而且已经获得了诺贝尔奖。

sentences.en: And he invited me to his house and I thought he wanted me to interview him.
sentences.zh: 他邀请我去了他家，我还以为他是想让我采访他呢。

sentences.en: This was such a huge honor.
sentences.zh: 这真是无上的荣耀。

sentences.en: I mean, everybody was so jealous in the magazine because he had chosen me to go and interview him.
sentences.zh: 我是说，杂志社里的每个人都嫉妒得要命，因为他选中我去采访他。

sentences.en: It was winter, and I drove raining all the way to that place, and he received me very kindly.
sentences.zh: 那是冬天，我冒着雨一路开车到那个地方，他非常亲切地接待了我。

sentences.en: He had lunch for me, a bottle of white wine.
sentences.zh: 他为我准备了午餐和一瓶白葡萄酒。

sentences.en: He showed me his collections.
sentences.zh: 他向我展示了他的藏品。

sentences.en: His collections now are considered art.
sentences.zh: 他的那些藏品现在都被视作艺术品了。

sentences.en: Then it was junk.
sentences.zh: 但在当时，那些只是破烂。

sentences.en: And then I said, okay, Don Paolo, I really need to do the interview because it's going to get dark soon and I need to get back.
sentences.zh: 然后我说，好吧，保罗叔叔，我真的得开始采访了，因为天快黑了，我得赶回去。

sentences.en: What interview, he said.
sentences.zh: 什么采访，他说。

sentences.en: Well, I came to interview you.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我是来采访你的。

sentences.en: Oh, no, my dear, I would never be interviewed by you.
sentences.zh: 哦，不，亲爱的，我绝不会接受你的采访。

sentences.en: You are the worst journalist in this country.
sentences.zh: 你是这个国家最糟糕的记者。

sentences.en: You put yourself always in the middle of everything.
sentences.zh: 你总是把自己卷进所有事情的中心。

sentences.en: You lie all the time.
sentences.zh: 你满嘴谎言。

sentences.en: And I'm sure that if you don't have a story, you make it up.
sentences.zh: 而且我敢肯定，要是你没有故事，你就会凭空捏造一个。

sentences.en: Why don't you switch to literature where all these defects are virtues?
sentences.zh: 你为什么不转行去写文学呢？在那里，所有这些缺点都会变成优点。

sentences.en: I should have paid attention, but I didn't.
sentences.zh: 我本该听进去的，但我没有。

sentences.en: Until many, many years later.
sentences.zh: 直到许多年以后。

sentences.en: Let's just take a step back.
sentences.zh: 我们先退一步讲。

sentences.en: You're in the home of this literary genius, and he tells you something that to most people would be crushing.
sentences.zh: 你身处这位文学巨匠的家中，而他对你说了一番对大多数人来说可能是毁灭性打击的话。

sentences.en: I was crushed too, of course.
sentences.zh: 我当然也被打击到了。

sentences.en: Of course I was crushed, but he said it very kindly.
sentences.zh: 我当然受到了打击，但他语气非常和善。

sentences.en: And I asked him then why he had invited me if he didn't want me to interview.
sentences.zh: 于是我问他，既然他不想接受采访，为什么还要邀请我。

sentences.en: He said because he liked what I wrote.
sentences.zh: 他说因为他喜欢我写的东西。

sentences.en: And sometimes he would make copies of my humorous articles and send them to his friends.
sentences.zh: 有时他还会复印我写的幽默文章，寄给他的朋友们。

sentences.en: And that's why he wanted to meet me.
sentences.zh: 这就是他想见我的原因。

sentences.en: But you did not listen to him at the time.
sentences.zh: 但你当时并没有听他的话。

sentences.en: No, I didn't.
sentences.zh: 是的，我没有。

sentences.en: And then two months later, we had the military coup.
sentences.zh: 然后两个月后，我们遭遇了军事政变。

sentences.en: So forget about any plans for the future.
sentences.zh: 所以，对未来的任何计划都化为乌有。

sentences.en: Everything was disrupted forever.
sentences.zh: 一切都被永远地打破了。

sentences.en: And it is one of those crossroads in your life in which you have to take a new direction that was completely not planned and not expected.
sentences.zh: 这是你人生中的那些十字路口之一，你不得不选择一个完全没有计划、始料未及的新方向。

sentences.en: And my career as a journalist ended there.
sentences.zh: 我作为记者的职业生涯就在那里结束了。

sentences.en: You had to go to Venezuela because there was a military coup.
sentences.zh: 因为发生了军事政变，你不得不去委内瑞拉。

sentences.en: What was the moment you knew it's time for me to go?
sentences.zh: 你是什么时候知道自己该离开的？

sentences.en: It took months and months, because although in Chile, the brutality started in 24 hours, and the Congress was dismissed indefinitely, there was censorship for everything,
sentences.zh: 这花了几个月的时间，因为虽然在智利，暴行在二十四小时内就开始了，国会被无限期解散，一切都受到了审查，

sentences.en: all civil rights were suspended, there was no habeas corpus, which means that a person can be arrested, and they don't have to give you any explanation.
sentences.zh: 所有公民权利都被中止，没有了人身保护令，这意味着一个人被捕了，他们甚至不需要给你任何解释。

sentences.en: and there is no hearing, there is no court.
sentences.zh: 没有听证会，也没有法庭。

sentences.en: You just go to jail or disappear.
sentences.zh: 你直接就被送进监狱或者人间蒸发。

sentences.en: You can be tortured and nothing happens.
sentences.zh: 你可能会遭受严刑拷打，而什么事都不会发生。

sentences.en: No one is accountable.
sentences.zh: 没有人会为此负责。

sentences.en: But although things happen very quickly in Chile, we got to know the consequences slowly because they don't affect you personally immediately.
sentences.zh: 但尽管智利的事情发生得极快，我们却是在慢慢意识到后果，因为它们不会立刻直接影响到你。

sentences.en: Of course, there were people who were persecuted and those were affected immediately, but most of the population wasn't.
sentences.zh: 当然，有些人遭到了迫害，他们立刻受到了影响，但绝大多数人并没有。

sentences.en: So you think, well, I can live with this.
sentences.zh: 所以你会想，好吧，我能忍受这个。

sentences.en: Well, it can't be that bad.
sentences.zh: 嗯，应该不会那么糟吧。

sentences.en: No, it's impossible.
sentences.zh: 不，这不可能。

sentences.en: You are in denial for a long time because you don't want things to change so much.
sentences.zh: 你在很长一段时间里都在逃避现实，因为你不想让生活发生如此巨大的改变。

sentences.en: And then one day it hits you personally.
sentences.zh: 直到有一天，现实重重地砸在你头上。

sentences.en: And then it's the time when you say, okay, I'm done.
sentences.zh: 那就是你对自己说，好吧，我受够了的时候。

sentences.en: For me, it was several things.
sentences.zh: 对我和说，原因有很多。

sentences.en: I was, at the beginning, I was hiding people in my house because we didn't know the consequences.
sentences.zh: 一开始，我在家里藏匿别人，因为我们不知道后果会怎样。

sentences.en: We had no idea that if that person was arrested and forced to say where they had been, I would be arrested.
sentences.zh: 我们根本不知道，如果那个人被捕并被迫招认去过哪里，我也会被捕。

sentences.en: Maybe my children would be tortured in front of me.
sentences.zh: 也许我的孩子会在我面前遭受虐待。

sentences.en: But you learn that later.
sentences.zh: 但这些你是后来才知道的。

sentences.en: And then by the time I was directly threatened, then I said, okay, I'm leaving.
sentences.zh: 直到我直接受到了威胁，我才说，好吧，我要走了。

sentences.en: And my idea was that I was going to leave for a couple of months and then come back.
sentences.zh: 我当时的打算是离开几个月就回来。

sentences.en: So I went alone to Venezuela.
sentences.zh: 所以我独自一人去了委内瑞拉。

sentences.en: And then a month later, my husband realized that I shouldn't go back.
sentences.zh: 一个月后，我丈夫意识到我不该再回去了。

sentences.en: And so he left.
sentences.zh: 于是他动身了。

sentences.en: He just closed the door, locked the entrance door of the house with everything it contained, and left to reunite with me in Venezuela.
sentences.zh: 他只是关上门，把家里所有的东西锁在门里，然后离开，去委内瑞拉和我会合。

sentences.en: We never saw that house again, and everything it contained was lost, which doesn't matter at all because I don't remember what was in there.
sentences.zh: 我们再也没有见过那栋房子，里面的一切都失去了，这其实完全无所谓，因为我已经记不清里面有什么了。

sentences.en: But I do remember the moment when I crossed the Andes in the plane.
sentences.zh: 但我确实记得我坐飞机飞越安第斯山脉的那一刻。

sentences.en: I cried in the plane because I knew somehow instinctively that this was a threshold, that everything had changed, definitely changed.
sentences.zh: 我在飞机上哭了，因为我凭直觉知道这是一个分水岭，一切都变了，彻底变了。

sentences.en: How did you explain it to your children?
sentences.zh: 你是怎么向孩子们解释这一切的？

sentences.en: I didn't, and that's my crime.
sentences.zh: 我没有，这就是我的过错。

sentences.en: We tried to protect the children from fear.
sentences.zh: 我们试图保护孩子们免受恐惧的侵害。

sentences.en: We were living in fear, and fear is a very pervasive thing that changes a society and changes the way people behave with each other and changes you inside.
sentences.zh: 我们生活在恐惧之中，恐惧是一种无孔不入的东西，它改变了一个社会，改变了人与人之间的相处方式，也从内部改变了你。

sentences.en: Something breaks inside you.
sentences.zh: 你的内心有什么东西碎了。

sentences.en: And we didn't want our children to know about torture, about people disappearing,
sentences.zh: 我们不想让孩子们知道酷刑，知道有人失踪，

sentences.en: But they were aware it was suddenly the teacher, two guys would come into the classroom and take the teacher away.
sentences.zh: 但他们是有所察觉的，突然之间老师……两名男子会走进教室把老师带走。

sentences.en: So the children would see it, but there was no explanation.
sentences.zh: 所以孩子们是能看到的，但没有任何解释。

sentences.en: And so when we left, the idea was, oh, we are going to Venezuela.
sentences.zh: 因此当我们离开时，我们的想法是，哦，我们要去委内瑞拉。

sentences.en: That's what my husband said.
sentences.zh: 我丈夫是这么说的。

sentences.en: We are going to Venezuela to see mommy.
sentences.zh: 我们要去委内瑞拉看妈妈。

sentences.en: So it took a while for them to understand that we were staying, that we were refugees, and that probably we would not go back, and they had to adapt.
sentences.zh: 所以他们花了很长时间才明白我们要留下来，我们是难民，而且我们可能不会回去了，他们必须适应这一切。

sentences.en: They had to get along with everybody else and just forget about what was behind.
sentences.zh: 他们必须和所有人融洽相处，把过去的事情抛在脑后。

sentences.en: After the break, Isabel tells me about the years she spent writing daily letters to her mother.
sentences.zh: 休息过后，伊莎贝尔将向我讲述她当年每天给母亲写信的日子。

sentences.en: We were very intimate and open, absolutely open in the letters.
sentences.zh: 我们在信里非常亲密和坦诚，毫无保留。

sentences.en: And when I went to visit, in a week we would feel like uncomfortable with each other because in person we didn't have the same openness that we had in writing.
sentences.zh: 而当我前去探望时，不到一周我们就会感到彼此生疏，因为在现实中我们无法像在书信中那样畅所欲言。

sentences.en: I'm Wena Liu.
sentences.zh: 我是刘文娜。

sentences.en: I write the game Connections, one of the puzzles from New York Times games.
sentences.zh: 我是《纽约时报》游戏板块拼字游戏《Connections》的创作者之一。

sentences.en: And I love horror movies.
sentences.zh: 我热爱恐怖电影。

sentences.en: I love my dog.
sentences.zh: 我爱我的狗狗。

sentences.en: And I love trying to trick you.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢尝试捉弄你们。

sentences.en: I'm Sam Mazursky, and I create the game Spelling Bee and Letterboxd on a daily basis.
sentences.zh: 我是萨姆·马苏斯基，我每天负责制作《Spelling Bee》和《Letterboxd》游戏。

sentences.en: And I have this thing called promesthesia.
sentences.zh: 我有一种叫做联觉的奇特体验。

sentences.en: I see color when I'm listening to music.
sentences.zh: 我在听音乐时能看到颜色。

sentences.en: New York Times games are made by people, like the ones you just heard from.
sentences.zh: 《纽约时报》的游戏是由活生生的人制作的，就像刚才你听到声音的那些人一样。

sentences.en: Go to nytimes.com slash games to start playing today.
sentences.zh: 访问 nytimes.com 休闲游戏频道，今天就开始玩吧。

sentences.en: So you wrote your first novel, House of the Spirits, at the age of 39.
sentences.zh: 所以你三十九岁时写了你的第一部小说《幽灵之家》。

sentences.en: In Venezuela.
sentences.zh: 在委内瑞拉。

sentences.en: And I think a lot of people have a feeling that at a certain point, maybe it's too late for doing the thing that they want to do, they were meant to do,
sentences.zh: 我想很多人都会有一种感觉，那就是在某个特定的人生阶段，去做他们想做的事、本该去做的事、一直梦想去做的事，也许已经太晚了，

sentences.en: they've always dreamed of doing.
sentences.zh: 他们一直梦想着去做的事。

sentences.en: When you got to that point where you started to write a letter to your grandfather that then turned into this incredible novel, did you think, what am I doing here?
sentences.zh: 当你到了那个阶段，开始给祖父写信，而这封信后来变成了一部不可思议的小说时，你有没有想过，我在这里干什么？

sentences.en: Like, this is not, I'm 39 years old, I'm not going to become a novelist at this age.
sentences.zh: 比如说，这不对劲，我已经三十九岁了，我不可能在这个年纪成为小说家。

sentences.en: I didn't think about age.
sentences.zh: 我没有考虑过年龄问题。

sentences.en: I was feeling that my life was going nowhere, that I had lived for 39 years, almost 40 years, and I had nothing to show for it except my two children.
sentences.zh: 我当时觉得我的人生毫无进展，我活了三十九岁，快四十岁了，除了两个孩子，什么也没有留下。

sentences.en: And I was very bored administering a school in a country that was not my own country, feeling very alien in many ways, like a visitor, and a visitor in life, in a way.
sentences.zh: 我很厌烦在一个不属于我的国家管理一所学校，在很多方面我都觉得自己像个局外人，像个访客，在某种程度上就像是一个人生的过客。

sentences.en: And so this letter that eventually turned into the book was like opening a vein and bleed out all that I was holding.
sentences.zh: 所以这封最终变成书的信，就像是划开血管，把压抑在我心中的一切全都释放出来。

sentences.en: And I think it was an exercise in longing.
sentences.zh: 我认为这是一次关于渴望的练习。

sentences.en: I wanted to go back.
sentences.zh: 我想回去。

sentences.en: I wanted to recover the country I had lost, my friends, my job, the life I had before.
sentences.zh: 我想找回我失去的国家，我的朋友们，我的工作，我以前的生活。

sentences.en: And in that attempt of recovering things that I had lost, I started bringing in the anecdotes of my grandfather, my country, the Del Valle family.
sentences.zh: 在试图找回失去之物的过程中，我开始融入我祖父的轶事、我的祖国、德尔瓦莱家族的故事。

sentences.en: And they started, these people, it was a whole village that came to the kitchen counter where I was writing and populated the pages.
sentences.zh: 他们开始涌现，这些人，整个村庄的人都来到了我写作时的厨房案台前，填满了书页。

sentences.en: I wasn't thinking.
sentences.zh: 我当时没有在思考。

sentences.en: I didn't have a plan.
sentences.zh: 我没有计划。

sentences.en: I didn't have an outline of any kind.
sentences.zh: 我没有任何形式的大纲。

sentences.en: I didn't know how to edit anything.
sentences.zh: 我不知道怎么去编辑任何东西。

sentences.en: To the point that when the book was finished and my husband, who was a civil engineer, read it, he said the only thing that he noticed was that the dates didn't match.
sentences.zh: 以至于当书写完后，身为土木工程师的丈夫读了它，他说他唯一注意到的就是日期对不上。

sentences.en: And then you had a character in page 20 that was 18 years old and in page 300 was still 18 years old.
sentences.zh: 然后你在第二0页有个角色十八岁，到了第三百页他还是十八岁。

sentences.en: What happened?
sentences.zh: 怎么回事？

sentences.en: this person didn't age.
sentences.zh: 这个人怎么不长岁数。

sentences.en: So he created a sort of map on the wall with the dates and the characters and what was happening.
sentences.zh: 于是他在墙上制作了一种地图，标上了日期、人物以及正在发生的事情。

sentences.en: And then I could organize it a little bit.
sentences.zh: 然后我才能稍微整理一下。

sentences.en: But I knew nothing about what I was.
sentences.zh: 但我对自己所做的事一无所知。

sentences.en: I didn't have an idea.
sentences.zh: 我完全没有概念。

sentences.en: You say you had a feeling that your life was going nowhere.
sentences.zh: 你说你曾觉得你的人生毫无进展。

sentences.en: You had nothing to show for it other than your two children.
sentences.zh: 除了两个孩子，你什么也没留下。

sentences.en: I think if I felt that way, I would be overwhelmed.
sentences.zh: 我想如果我有这种感觉，我会被压垮的。

sentences.en: And I don't know that I would be able to start anything.
sentences.zh: 我不知道自己是否有能力开始做任何事。

sentences.en: I'm wondering if you could talk about that feeling a little bit more.
sentences.zh: 我想知道你能不能多谈谈那种感觉。

sentences.en: I was loSt. I was bored.
sentences.zh: 我迷失了。我很厌烦。

sentences.en: I think I was somehow depressed.
sentences.zh: 我想我当时在某种程度上抑郁了。

sentences.en: Yeah, I didn't want that kind of life.
sentences.zh: 是的，我不想过那种生活。

sentences.en: But one thing has been always in my life, writing.
sentences.zh: 但我的生活中一直有一件事，那就是写作。

sentences.en: Writing as a journalist, writing letters to my mother, writing to my grandfather, always writing.
sentences.zh: 作为记者写作，给母亲写信，给祖父写信，一直在写。

sentences.en: I think that my way of getting over things, of understanding, of exploring my own soul, my past, and also, most important, of remembering, is writing.
sentences.zh: 我认为我超越困境、理解世界、探索自己的灵魂与过去，以及最重要的一点——铭记的方式，就是写作。

sentences.en: When my daughter died,
sentences.zh: 当我的女儿去世时，

sentences.en: that was the worst time in my whole life.
sentences.zh: 那是我一生中最糟糕的时刻。

sentences.en: And it was a very long time also.
sentences.zh: 而且那段痛苦持续了非常久。

sentences.en: It lasted more than a year the only way that i could understand it and cope with it was writing and i wrote a book
sentences.zh: 持续了一年多，我唯一能理解它并与之共存的方式就是写作，我写了一本书。

sentences.en: it's been a little more than 30 years since you published that memoir that you just referred to
sentences.zh: 距离你出版刚才提到的那本回忆录已经过去三十多年了，

sentences.en: paula which is named after your daughter it's about your life with her and the situation you
sentences.zh: 也就是以你女儿名字命名的《宝拉》，书里讲述了你与她共度的生活，以及她陷入昏迷很长时间后最终离世的遭遇，

sentences.en: found yourself in where she was in a coma for quite a long time and then she eventually passed
sentences.zh: 这段经历让你陷入了困境。

sentences.en: I am curious how your grief has changed after or evolved in the 30 years since you lost your daughter.
sentences.zh: 我很好奇，在你失去女儿之后的这三十年里，你的悲痛是如何改变或演变的？

sentences.en: I feel my daughter like a companion.
sentences.zh: 我把女儿当成伴侣一样感受她的存在。

sentences.en: I have her photograph on her wedding day and my mother in a wedding dress when she put it on when she was 80.
sentences.zh: 洗手池边放着两张照片，一张是她婚礼当天的照片，另一张是我母亲八十岁时穿上婚纱的照片。

sentences.en: I have these two photographs on the sink where I brush my teeth every morning and every night.
sentences.zh: 每天早晨和晚上我刷牙时，都会看到洗手池上的这两张照片。

sentences.en: So I said, good morning, good evening.
sentences.zh: 所以我会说，早安，晚安。

sentences.en: They are always with me.
sentences.zh: 她们一直陪伴着我。

sentences.en: And I'm constantly in touch with Paula.
sentences.zh: 我一直在与宝拉保持着精神上的联系。

sentences.en: I don't believe in ghosts.
sentences.zh: 我不相信鬼魂。

sentences.en: I don't see her as an apparition.
sentences.zh: 我不认为她是以幽灵的形式存在。

sentences.en: And I don't believe that after I die, I will go through a tunnel of light and I will find her at the other end.
sentences.zh: 我也不相信在我死后，我会穿过一条光之隧道，然后在尽头找到她。

sentences.en: But she lives in me.
sentences.zh: 但她活在我体内。

sentences.en: And there's a continuation.
sentences.zh: 生命是延续的。

sentences.en: The grandmother, the mother, the daughter, the granddaughter.
sentences.zh: 祖母、母亲、女儿、孙女。

sentences.en: We're all linked in a chain.
sentences.zh: 我们都被一根链条紧紧相连。

sentences.en: And we all live in each other, in a way.
sentences.zh: 从某种意义上说，我们都活在彼此心中。

sentences.en: I get the impression, I think you've said this maybe before, that it's a book that still resonates greatly with people after all this time.
sentences.zh: 我有一种印象——我想你以前可能也说过——时隔这么久，这本书依然能深深引发人们的共鸣。

sentences.en: I have written 30 books.
sentences.zh: 我已经写了30本书。

sentences.en: and this is the one that has had in time the greatest response from the readers.
sentences.zh: 而这是随着时间推移，收获读者反响最大的一本。

sentences.en: Everybody has losses.
sentences.zh: 每个人都会经历失去。

sentences.en: It doesn't have to be a child.
sentences.zh: 对象不一定非得是孩子。

sentences.en: It can be divorce.
sentences.zh: 也可以是离婚。

sentences.en: You lose your job.
sentences.zh: 你失去了工作。

sentences.en: You lose your health, your parents.
sentences.zh: 你失去了健康、失去了父母。

sentences.en: And people connect to the loss, no matter what loss it is.
sentences.zh: 无论失去的是什么，人们都能对这种痛苦感同身受。

sentences.en: In this case, it's Paula.
sentences.zh: 就这本书而言，是保拉。

sentences.en: and I get the most extraordinary letters.
sentences.zh: 我收到了最多非同寻常的信件。

sentences.en: That's the kind of reward that very few writers get.
sentences.zh: 这是极少数作家才能获得的奖赏。

sentences.en: I've been very, very lucky.
sentences.zh: 我一直非常非常幸运。

sentences.en: Speaking of letters, your first novel, of course, started as a letter.
sentences.zh: 说到信件，你的第一部小说，当然也是从一封信开始的。

sentences.en: Your memoir was a letter to your daughter.
sentences.zh: 你的回忆录就是写给你女儿的一封信。

sentences.en: And I'm wondering if we could talk about the exercise of writing letters for you.
sentences.zh: 我想我们可以聊聊书信这种形式对你的意义。

sentences.en: It's just not something that people do anymore.
sentences.zh: 这已经不再是人们会做的事情了。

sentences.en: Unfortunately, it's a lost art.
sentences.zh: 不幸的是，这是一门失传的艺术。

sentences.en: Language has shrunk to nothing because of the email.
sentences.zh: 因为电子邮件，语言已经缩水得所剩无几。

sentences.en: And we write like a telegram.
sentences.zh: 我们写信就像发电报一样。

sentences.en: We communicate with very few words and very poor imagery.
sentences.zh: 我们用极少的词汇和极其匮乏的意象进行交流。

sentences.en: But I grew up writing to my mother every single day because my mother was married to a diplomat.
sentences.zh: 但我从小就每天给母亲写信，因为我母亲嫁给了一位外交官。

sentences.en: And when I was 16, we separated and we never lived together again.
sentences.zh: 在我16岁那年，我们分居了，就再也没有一起生活过。

sentences.en: So we got the habit of writing to each other every single day.
sentences.zh: 所以我们养成了每天给对方写信的习惯。

sentences.en: I would go through the day noticing what I would write to my mother in the evening.
sentences.zh: 我会在白天留意各种事物，好在晚上写信告诉母亲。

sentences.en: So I was present in the day, taking mental notes of what I was living, I was seeing, I was thinking, I was dreaming, of the conversations, the encounters of everything,
sentences.zh: 所以我能专注于当下，在脑海中记下我的生活、所见、所思、所想、所梦，以及所有的对话和遭遇，

sentences.en: so that I would have some material for the evening letter to my mother.
sentences.zh: 这样我好为给母亲的晚间信件积累一些素材。

sentences.en: Now, she died in 2018.
sentences.zh: 她于2018年去世了。

sentences.en: And I tried for a while to keep on writing to her as if she was alive, but it didn't work.
sentences.zh: 有一段时间，我试图继续给她写信，就好像她还活着一样，但行不通。

sentences.en: It was very artificial.
sentences.zh: 那太不自然了。

sentences.en: But since then, I go through life like in a state of daydreaming.
sentences.zh: 但从那以后，我过生活就像处于白日梦的状态中一样。

sentences.en: I don't notice anything anymore because I don't have to write about it.
sentences.zh: 我不再注意到任何事情，因为我不再需要把它们写下来了。

sentences.en: It's sad.
sentences.zh: 这很令人难过。

sentences.en: I have collected my mother's letters and my letters since 1987.
sentences.zh: 我收集了我母亲和我的信件，从1987年开始。

sentences.en: They are separated in boxes by year.
sentences.zh: 它们按年份装在不同的盒子里。

sentences.en: Some of the boxes have 600, 800 letters.
sentences.zh: 有些盒子里有600封、800封信。

sentences.en: So in total, we have calculated that I have around 24,000 letters.
sentences.zh: 所以总的来说，我们计算过，我大约有24,000封信。

sentences.en: Can you imagine the volume of that?
sentences.zh: 你能想象那是怎样庞大的体量吗？

sentences.en: That's so many words to have exchanged with another person.
sentences.zh: 那是与另一个人交流过如此之多的字句。

sentences.en: What did you learn about her from these letters?
sentences.zh: 从这些信中，你了解到了她怎样的为人？

sentences.en: You know, it's very interesting because we were very intimate and open, absolutely open in the letters.
sentences.zh: 你知道，这非常有趣，因为我们在信中极其亲密和坦诚，毫无保留。

sentences.en: And when I went to visit, in a week we would feel like uncomfortable with each other because in person we didn't have the same openness that we had in writing.
sentences.zh: 而当我去探望她时，不出一个星期我们就会感到彼此有些局促，因为面对面时我们没有在信中那种坦诚。

sentences.en: I don't know.
sentences.zh: 我不知道。

sentences.en: Things got in the way when we were together that didn't when we were writing.
sentences.zh: 当我们在一起时，总有些东西会成为阻碍，而写信时则不会。

sentences.en: So I got to know my mother in ways that I don't know anybody else, not even my children.
sentences.zh: 所以我以一种我不了解任何其他人的方式了解了我的母亲，甚至连我的孩子们都比不上。

sentences.en: Everything about her, her health, her dreams, her longings, her disappointments, her fights with my stepfather, the reconciliations, everything.
sentences.zh: 关于她的一切，她的健康、她的梦想、她的渴望、她的失望、她与我继父的争吵、他们的和解，事无巨细。

sentences.en: We talked about money, sex, religion, you name it.
sentences.zh: 我们聊金钱、性、宗教，你能想到的都有。

sentences.en: And she had a sort of Chilean sarcasm that I loved.
sentences.zh: 她有一种我非常喜欢的智利式的讽刺幽默。

sentences.en: And we connected through that, too.
sentences.zh: 我们也通过这种方式产生了共鸣。

sentences.en: But that works in a letter.
sentences.zh: 但那在信里管用。

sentences.en: And then in person can be offensive.
sentences.zh: 而面对面时可能会具有攻击性。

sentences.en: Do you feel like there's just something inherent in, as you say, the intimacy of letter writing,
sentences.zh: 你是否觉得，正如你所说，书信往来的亲密感中有一种与生俱来的东西，

sentences.en: the access you have to someone's inner feelings that just cannot be replicated when you're with that person, for the most part?
sentences.zh: 也就是你能够触及某人内心深处的情感，而这种体验在绝大多数情况下，当你和那个人在一起时是无法复制的？

sentences.en: Well, maybe some people can.
sentences.zh: 嗯，也许有些人可以吧。

sentences.en: I cannot.
sentences.zh: 我不行。

sentences.en: You know what?
sentences.zh: 你知道吗？

sentences.en: I married Roger.
sentences.zh: 我嫁给了罗杰。

sentences.en: I mean, we've been together for six years.
sentences.zh: 我是说，我们已经在一起六年了。

sentences.en: This is your third husband.
sentences.zh: 这是你的第三任丈夫。

sentences.en: My third husband.
sentences.zh: 我的第三任丈夫。

sentences.en: Not the last one, but the third.
sentences.zh: 不是最后一个，但确实是第三个。

sentences.en: Got it.
sentences.zh: 明白了。

sentences.en: And so when we are separated physically, he writes to me the most tender and beautiful text, and I can do that too.
sentences.zh: 所以当我们物理上分开时，他会给我写最温柔、最美丽的短信，我也能做到这一点。

sentences.en: But when we are in person, I just can't say it.
sentences.zh: 但当我们在现实中面对面时，我就是说不出口。

sentences.en: It feels awkward.
sentences.zh: 感觉怪怪的。

sentences.en: It feels awkward.
sentences.zh: 感觉很尴尬。

sentences.en: In Spanish, you say, for example, tú eres la luz de mis ojos.
sentences.zh: 在西班牙语里，你会说，例如，tú eres la luz de mis ojos。

sentences.en: You are the light of my eyes.
sentences.zh: 你是我眼中的光。

sentences.en: In English, it sounds awful.
sentences.zh: 在英语里，听起来糟透了。

sentences.en: I can't say that in person to anybody, but I can write it.
sentences.zh: 我无法当面对任何人说出这话，但我可以把它写下来。

sentences.en: Is it true that Roger reached out to you after hearing you on the radio by writing you a letter?
sentences.zh: 罗杰是在收音机里听到你的声音后，给你写了一封信来联系你的，对吗？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Well, an email.
sentences.zh: 嗯，是一封电子邮件。

sentences.en: An email.
sentences.zh: 一封电子邮件。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好吧。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: He heard me on NPR.
sentences.zh: 他在NPR上听到了我的节目。

sentences.en: I was seeing him sitting down, taking out a piece of paper, writing it out of there, okay, an email.
sentences.zh: 我当时想象着他坐下来，拿出一张纸，从那上面写信——好吧，是一封电子邮件。

sentences.en: He sent me an email, sent an email to my foundation saying that whatever, and very brief.
sentences.zh: 他给我发了一封电子邮件，发给我基金会说七七八八的事，非常简短。

sentences.en: And at the end, it said that he was willing to go anywhere, anytime to meet me.
sentences.zh: 最后他说，他愿意随时随地去任何地方见我。

sentences.en: But I answered politely because I receive many emails daily, and I don't keep a correspondence with everybody.
sentences.zh: 但我礼貌地回复了，因为我每天收到很多邮件，我不会跟所有人保持通信。

sentences.en: I just answer the first one.
sentences.zh: 我只是回复了第一封。

sentences.en: But he kept writing every morning and every evening for six months.
sentences.zh: 但他连续六个月，每天早晚都坚持写信。

sentences.en: I mean, really stubborn, the guy.
sentences.zh: 我是说，这家伙真的很顽固。

sentences.en: And he didn't sound like the normal stalker.
sentences.zh: 而且他听起来不像那种普通的跟踪狂。

sentences.en: He sounded like a very transparent guy, actually.
sentences.zh: 实际上，他听起来像个非常坦诚的人。

sentences.en: So when I went to New York, I went to a conference for reproductive rights.
sentences.zh: 所以当我去纽约时，我去参加了一个关于生殖权利的会议。

sentences.en: I met him.
sentences.zh: 我见到了他。

sentences.en: And in two days, he proposed and said that he would marry me eventually, no matter what.
sentences.zh: 短短两天内，他就向我求婚，并说无论如何最终都要娶我。

sentences.en: But he was living in New York, and I was living here.
sentences.zh: 但他住在纽约，而我住在加州。

sentences.en: So he, at some point, sold his house, gave away everything he had, and moved to California with two bikes, his clothes, and some crystal glasses for some reason.
sentences.zh: 所以他后来卖掉了房子，送走了他拥有的一切，带着两辆自行车、他的衣服和不知为何的一些水晶杯，搬到了加利福尼亚。

sentences.en: I don't know why.
sentences.zh: 我不知道为什么。

sentences.en: That's quite powerful.
sentences.zh: 这很有力量感。

sentences.en: You convinced a man to just get rid of his entire life and move across the country.
sentences.zh: 你居然说服了一个男人抛弃他整个人生，横跨整个国家搬过来。

sentences.en: I didn't ask him to do it.
sentences.zh: 我没有要求他这么做。

sentences.en: He did it.
sentences.zh: 是他自己做的。

sentences.en: No, you didn't need to, clearly.
sentences.zh: 不，显然你不需要要求。

sentences.en: But you know what is interesting, Gilberto, is that shortly before that, a couple of years before,
sentences.zh: 但你知道有趣的是什么吗，吉尔伯托，就在那之前不久，也就是几年之前，

sentences.en: I divorced from my second husband, Willie Gordon, and I sold my house and gave away everything also.
sentences.zh: 我与第二任丈夫威利·戈登离了婚，我也卖掉了房子，送走了所有东西。

sentences.en: Because I moved to a very small house with my dog, and I didn't need anything.
sentences.zh: 因为我和我的狗搬进了一栋很小的房子里，我什么都不需要。

sentences.en: So we both, in a way, started from scratch together, which was a very good thing to do.
sentences.zh: 所以从某种意义上说，我们俩一起从零开始，这是一件非常棒的事情。

sentences.en: No baggage, at least material baggage.
sentences.zh: 没有包袱，至少没有物质包袱。

sentences.en: Yeah, no material baggage.
sentences.zh: 是的，没有物质包袱。

sentences.en: I read an interview with you where you said that when you got a divorce in your early 70s, some people around you thought, maybe this is a little crazy.
sentences.zh: 我读过你的一篇采访，你在其中提到，当你七出头离婚时，你身边的一些人觉得，这可能有点疯狂。

sentences.en: How did that feel to you at that stage in your life?
sentences.zh: 在你人生的那个阶段，你对此有什么感觉？

sentences.en: Well, I was 74 years old.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我当时74岁了。

sentences.en: We had been together for 28 years.
sentences.zh: 我们已经在一起28年了。

sentences.en: I had loved that man a lot.
sentences.zh: 我曾深爱过那个男人。

sentences.en: But, you know, you never know why love ends at some point.
sentences.zh: 但是，你知道，你永远不会知道为什么爱会在某个时刻消逝。

sentences.en: And it isn't sudden.
sentences.zh: 这不是突然发生的。

sentences.en: It was a slow deterioration that took years and a lot of therapy to try to fix it until we realized we couldn't fix it.
sentences.zh: 那是一个缓慢恶化的过程，经历了多年以及大量的心理治疗试图去修复，直到我们意识到无法修复为止。

sentences.en: And so we divorced, and many people said, well, you've invested all these years.
sentences.zh: 于是我们离婚了，许多人说，好吧，你投入了这么多年。

sentences.en: What's wrong?
sentences.zh: 怎么了？

sentences.en: What is so bad that you can't be together?
sentences.zh: 到底有什么大不了的，让你们无法在一起？

sentences.en: Nothing was really very bad, but I thought that it takes more courage to stay in a bad relationship than to start anew alone.
sentences.zh: 其实并没有什么特别糟糕的事，但我认为，维持一段糟糕的感情比孤身一人重新开始需要更大的勇气。

sentences.en: You really have to be very courageous to decide that you are going to spend the rest of the few years you have with a man that doesn't love you
sentences.zh: 你真的必须非常勇敢，才能做出这样的决定：你要和一个不爱你的人，

sentences.en: and in a relationship that is not working.
sentences.zh: 以及在一段没有结果的感情中度过你余下不多的岁月。

sentences.en: It's much better to just be alone.
sentences.zh: 独自一人要好得多。

sentences.en: So that's what I did.
sentences.zh: 所以我就是这么做的。

sentences.en: You grew up in Chile, lived your young adult life there, and then you've been in America for several decades.
sentences.zh: 你在智利长大，在那里度过了年轻时代，然后在美利坚生活了几十年。

sentences.en: You said during a speech you gave in 2018 when you accepted an award from the National Book Foundation, I was in the audience that night, you said,
sentences.zh: 你在2018年接受国家图书基金会颁奖时发表了一次演讲——我那天晚上也在观众席中——你说过，

sentences.en: although I am critical of many things about this country, I am proud to be an American citizen.
sentences.zh: 尽管我对这个国家的很多方面持批判态度，但我很骄傲能成为一名美国公民。

sentences.en: I'm wondering how your thoughts about your citizenship have changed, if they have at all.
sentences.zh: 我想知道，你对自身公民身份的看法是否发生了变化，哪怕有一点点？

sentences.en: They have not changed.
sentences.zh: 没有变。

sentences.en: Over the past year, I am really critical.
sentences.zh: 在过去的一年里，我确实持批判态度。

sentences.en: I am disgusted at a lot of stuff that is happening today, and I'm willing to stand and work to make this country what it should be.
sentences.zh: 我对当今发生的很多事情感到厌恶，但我愿意挺身而出，努力让这个国家成为它本该成为的样子。

sentences.en: I want this country to be compassionate and open and generous and happy, as it has always been, a beacon for the rest of the world.
sentences.zh: 我希望这个国家充满同情心、开放、慷慨而快乐，就像它一直以来那样，成为世界其他地方的一座明灯。

sentences.en: Since 2016, I believe, your foundation has worked with refugees, especially those along the southern border of the United States.
sentences.zh: 我想自2016年以来，你的基金会一直致力于帮助难民，尤其是美国南部边境的难民。

sentences.en: Has the work that your foundation does, has it become more difficult in recent months?
sentences.zh: 你基金会所做的工作，在最近几个月变得更加困难了吗？

sentences.en: Yes, very difficult.
sentences.zh: 是的，非常困难。

sentences.en: And there is a lot of really cruel things happening at the border that most of the American public doesn't know about, doesn't know the extent or the brutality.
sentences.zh: 边境正在发生许多非常残酷的事情，大多数美国公众对此并不了解，也不知道其严重程度或残酷性。

sentences.en: And my foundation works with that.
sentences.zh: 我的基金会正是为此而工作的。

sentences.en: We work with women mostly and children, the most vulnerable people.
sentences.zh: 我们主要帮助妇女和儿童，也就是最脆弱的人群。

sentences.en: And it's very sad.
sentences.zh: 这非常令人难过。

sentences.en: And I don't know for how long we will be able to do this.
sentences.zh: 我不知道我们还能坚持做多久。

sentences.en: What would stop you?
sentences.zh: 什么会阻止你？

sentences.en: What would get in your way?
sentences.zh: 什么会成为你的阻碍？

sentences.en: Well, of course, if the work is forbidden, if the people whom we help are targeted and their safety in any way is at risk, then that's as much as you can do.
sentences.zh: 当然，如果这项工作被禁止，如果我们帮助的人成为攻击目标，并且他们的安全受到任何威胁，那你就只能做到这一步了。

sentences.en: You have this humanitarian work that you're doing over here and then over here every day for eight, ten, however many hours you're in front of the keyboard and you're writing.
sentences.zh: 你一边做着这样的人道主义工作，另一边每天花八个小时、十个小时，无论多少时间坐在键盘前写作。

sentences.en: Are those two things connected in your mind or do they exist in separate worlds?
sentences.zh: 在你的脑海里，这两件事是有联系的，还是存在于两个不同的世界？

sentences.en: They exist separately because I don't do any social preaching, let's say, or political activity in my writing.
sentences.zh: 它们是分开存在的，因为我在写作中不做任何社会说教，比方说，也不搞政治活动。

sentences.en: I write fiction.
sentences.zh: 我写的是虚构小说。

sentences.en: If I write a nonfiction book, then I feel that I am allowed to say whatever I want, to preach, to teach, to whatever.
sentences.zh: 如果我写纪实作品，我觉得我就可以畅所欲言、说教、授业，或者做任何我想做的事。

sentences.en: But if it's fiction, I just want to tell a story.
sentences.zh: 但如果是小说，我只想讲一个故事。

sentences.en: And I don't want the storytelling to be tinted by ideology.
sentences.zh: 而且我不想让小说的叙事沾染上意识形态色彩。

sentences.en: I try to separate activism from literature.
sentences.zh: 我尽量把积极行动主义和文学分离开来。

sentences.en: And that's a conscious decision?
sentences.zh: 这是一个有意识的决定吗？

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Because I imagine given what you care about, what you're passionate about, the types of stories that you tell,
sentences.zh: 因为我想象着，鉴于你在乎的事、你充满热情的事以及你所讲述的故事类型，

sentences.en: that even if you're writing historical fiction or fiction set in the past, something will make its way in.
sentences.zh: 即使你写的是历史小说或以过去为背景的小说，有些东西也会渗透进来。

sentences.en: There will be parallels, even if that's not your intention.
sentences.zh: 会有相似之处，即使这不是你的本意。

sentences.en: Yeah, but I try to avoid it.
sentences.zh: 是的，但我尽量避免这种情况。

sentences.en: Sometimes things filter between the lines.
sentences.zh: 有时有些东西还是会字里行间地渗透出来。

sentences.en: But the best way to ruin a good novel is by trying to deliver a message.
sentences.zh: 但毁掉一本好小说的最好方法，就是试图去传达某种讯息。

sentences.en: You've said that you write sometimes as an act of nostalgia, clearly as an act of remembering.
sentences.zh: 你曾说过，你写作有时是出于一种怀旧，显然也是一种铭记的行为。

sentences.en: What, as you look to the future, what do you think you want to remember now?
sentences.zh: 当你展望未来时，你觉得你现在想记住什么？

sentences.en: Right now, I'm trying to be very present in the process of aging, because I think it's a fascinating time.
sentences.zh: 眼下，我正努力清醒地活在衰老的进程中，因为我认为这是一个迷人的时期。

sentences.en: And sort of taboo in this society where we live, people don't want to hear about aging.
sentences.zh: 在我们生活的这个社会里，这算是一种禁忌，人们不想听到关于衰老的事。

sentences.en: It's like ugly, and it can be, of course, but it can also be very liberating and a very wonderful journey.
sentences.zh: 它听起来很丑陋，当然也确实可能是这样，但它也可以非常解放，是一段非常美妙的旅程。

sentences.en: So I am trying to keep a record of this right now.
sentences.zh: 所以我现在正努力把这一切记录下来。

sentences.en: But I'm very interested in what's happening in the world also.
sentences.zh: 但我也对世界上正在发生的事情非常感兴趣。

sentences.en: So I think that political events like what we are living today in the United States cannot be analyzed or explained or understood in the moment.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为，像我们今天在美国所经历的这种政治事件，是无法在当下被分析、解释或理解的。

sentences.en: You have to look at it with the distance of time.
sentences.zh: 你必须用时间的距离去审视它。

sentences.en: That gives you some perspective.
sentences.zh: 这能带给你一些视角。

sentences.en: And I know this because I remember that I could not write about the military coup in Chile when it happened.
sentences.zh: 我深知这一点，因为我记得智利发生军事政变时，我根本写不出来。

sentences.en: I had all the information, but I couldn't write about it.
sentences.zh: 我掌握了所有的信息，但我就是写不出来。

sentences.en: I wrote The House of the Spirits many years later.
sentences.zh: 很多年后我才写了《幽灵之家》。

sentences.en: So I think that I hope to have enough time to be able to see what we are living today with some perspective.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为，我希望有足够的时间，能够带着一些视角来看待我们今天所经历的一切。

sentences.en: That's Isabel Allende.
sentences.zh: 那是伊莎贝尔·阿连德。

sentences.en: My name is Emilia Del Valle.
sentences.zh: 我的名字叫埃米莉亚·德尔瓦莱。
